title: Densest packings of two translates of a lattice in five dimensions: paper, Lean 4 formalization, certificate and verification programs
description:
We prove that no packing of unit balls in R^5 whose centres form two translates of a lattice is denser than the D5 lattice packing: if distinct points of Λ ∪ (Λ + b) are at distance at least 2, then the covolume of Λ is at least 16√2. Equality holds for exactly five pairs (Λ, b) up to congruence, giving three point sets: √2 D5, the uniform packing with Szöllősi's kissing configuration Q5, and Leech's 2-periodic layered packing with kissing configuration L5. Every Voronoi cell of such a set has volume at least 8√2.

preprintAndreanovKallusTwoPeriodicPackingD5/ holds the paper as a PDF; paper/ holds the LaTeX source (amsart) with three schematic figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball; MasterAndreanovKallusTwoPeriodicPackingD5_masterzipfinal2.zip holds every file of the repository. The proof reduces the bound to the vertices and edges of a locally finite polyhedron in the space of symmetric 6 × 6 matrices; up to symmetry it has 34 vertices, whose cones have 80,695 extreme rays in 480 orbits. cert/certificate.txt records this computation in exact arithmetic. checkers/ holds four independent checkers of the certificate (C, C++, Julia, Python) and two double-description enumerations of the extreme rays (C, Julia); cddlib and lrs recompute the rays as well. lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project whose theorem D5.certificate proves in the kernel the vertex and edge statements of the certificate, without native_decide, using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; the rank conditions, the completeness of the ray lists and the orbit decompositions are checked by the programs and are not formalized. The reduction and the equality case are proved by hand in the paper. run_all.sh runs every check.
